security_audit.summary: The reviewed findings are mostly static-analysis false positives from Markdown code fences, prose, and RegExp.exec usage. The only confirmed issues are low-severity third-party network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in the generated viewer template.

remediation.issue: The generated viewer depends on external CDN and font services.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js and required fonts locally, or clearly disclose that generated artifacts make third-party network requests.

content.value_statement: Creative coding can be hard to translate from an abstract visual idea into working interactive art. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create p5.js generative art with seeded variation and controls.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before writing the artwork implementation.
Uses p5.js templates for interactive browser-based generative art.
Builds seed controls so users can reproduce and explore variations.
Adds parameter sliders and color controls that match the artwork concept.
Supports particle systems, flow fields, noise fields, and procedural structures.
Produces self-contained HTML artifacts for browser or Claude artifact use.
limitations: Generated viewers load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless modified.
The skill does not verify copyright safety beyond instructing original creation.
Complex animations may need performance tuning for older devices.
It depends on the model to implement the final algorithm correctly.

use_cases.title: Prototype generative art concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a short visual idea into a reproducible p5.js artwork with tunable controls.

use_cases.title: Teach procedural art methods
use_cases.description: Show how seeded randomness, noise, particles, and parameters combine into visual systems.

use_cases.title: Create interactive visual assets
use_cases.description: Generate browser-ready visual experiments for presentations, portfolios, or design exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple generative artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a broad theme.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive algorithmic artwork about ocean currents. Include a short philosophy, seeded variation, and simple controls.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a visual system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create p5.js generative art using particles, flow fields, and warm colors. Make the seed controls and parameter sliders easy to use.

prompt_templates.title: Build a themed art artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece inspired by urban transit maps, but do not copy any existing map. Express the concept through paths, density, and motion.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a refined interactive series
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for variation and polish.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gallery-quality generative art artifact with seed presets, tuned parameters, and a clear explanation of how each control changes the system.

output_examples.input: Create generative art about wind moving through grass.
output: A concise algorithmic philosophy about directional force and organic response.
An interactive p5.js viewer with seed navigation, flow controls, and color settings.
A reproducible artwork where each seed changes the field and blade behavior.

output_examples.input: Make a particle system that feels like magnetic dust.
output: A conceptual description of attraction, repulsion, and accumulation.
A browser-ready artifact with particle count, field strength, and trail controls.
Seeded variations that preserve the same magnetic behavior with different layouts.

output_examples.input: Create an abstract piece based on city noise at night.
output: A visual system based on pulsing clusters, dark space, and controlled randomness.
Interactive parameters for density, pulse speed, contrast, and seed exploration.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual concept so the algorithm has a strong direction.
Use seeds and parameter controls to compare variations without losing reproducibility.
Review generated HTML for performance before sharing complex animated pieces.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to copy a living artist or an identifiable copyrighted artwork.
Do not remove seed controls if reproducible variation matters.
Do not request very high particle counts without testing browser performance.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates algorithmic art concepts and interactive p5.js HTML artifacts with seeded variations and controls.

faq.question: Can the artwork run in a browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The intended output is a self-contained HTML artifact that can run in a browser or Claude artifact view.

faq.question: Does it support reproducible outputs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeded randomness so the same seed can produce the same visual result.

faq.question: Can users adjust the artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes seed navigation, parameter sliders, color controls, reset actions, and related UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: The default template loads p5.js and fonts from external services. Authors can modify it to bundle those assets locally.

faq.question: Is it suitable for commercial artwork?
faq.answer: It can support original creative work, but users should review licensing, originality, and asset dependencies before commercial use.
